say.en: At audio frequencies an LC tank would need huge, heavy coils. Instead we can use only resistors and capacitors to produce the 180 degrees phase shift. In this lesson: Explain how three RC sections give 180 degrees.
Use f equals 1 over (2 pi RC the square root of 6).
State the minimum gain and the merits and demerits.

title.en: Working of the RC phase-shift oscillator

body.en: The amplifier (a CE stage or an inverting op-amp) gives 180°. Its output is fed back through three identical RC sections. A single RC section cannot shift the phase by 90° at a finite frequency, so three are used; at the oscillation frequency each gives 60°, total 180°. The loop phase is then 360°. For three equal sections $f = 1/(2\pi RC\sqrt6)$, and at that frequency the network attenuates the signal to $\beta = 1/29$, so the amplifier gain must be at least 29.

narration.en: Three RC sections each shift the phase by sixty degrees. The frequency is one over two pi R C root six, and the gain must be at least twenty-nine.
narration.kn: ಮೂರು RC ವಿಭಾಗಗಳು ತಲಾ 60° ಹಂತ ಸ್ಥಾನಾಂತರ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಆವೃತ್ತಿ f = 1/(2πRC√6); ವರ್ಧಕದ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ 29 ಇರಬೇಕು.

narration.en: Three RC sections shift the phase of the signal. At exactly one frequency, f0 = 1/(2π√6 RC), the total shift is 180°, which, with the 180° of the inverting amplifier, makes 360°. There the network passes only 1/29 of the signal, so the amplifier gain must be at least 29.
narration.kn: ಮೂರು RC ಭಾಗಗಳು ಹಂತವನ್ನು ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. f0 = 1/(2π√6 RC) ನಲ್ಲಿ ಒಟ್ಟು 180°; ವರ್ಧಕದ 180° ಸೇರಿ 360°. ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಜಾಲ 1/29 ಮಾತ್ರ ಹಾಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಲಾಭ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ 29.

body.en: *Merits*: no inductors, so it is simple, cheap and compact; it gives a good sine wave at audio and low frequencies (a few Hz to about 100 kHz). Demerits: tuning is awkward, because all three R or all three C must be changed together; it needs a high gain of 29; and the amplitude is less stable, so it is used mainly at fixed audio frequencies.

points.en: *Merits*: no coils, simple, good at audio frequencies

narration.en: The RC phase-shift oscillator is simple and good for audio, but it is hard to tune because three components must change together.

say.en: Let us work this out together. An RC phase-shift oscillator uses R equals 10 k ohms and C equals 0.01 microfarads in each section. Find its frequency.
RC equals 10 to the power 4 times 10 to the power minus 8 equals 10 to the power minus 4 seconds.
2 pi RC the square root of 6 equals 2 pi times 10 to the power minus 4 times 2.449 equals 1.539e-03 seconds.
f equals 649.7 hertz.
So the answer is About 650 hertz.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Design an RC phase-shift oscillator for 1 kilohertz using C equals 10 nanofarads.
R equals 1 over (2 pi f C the square root of 6).
R equals 1 over (2 pi times 1000 times 10 to the power minus 8 times 2.449) equals 6497 ohms.
Use R is approximately 6.5 k ohms (nearest standard 6.8 k ohms gives about 955 hertz), with an amplifier gain of at least 29.
So the answer is R is approximately 6.5 k ohms.
